us20_aid.topic: US government channels to Israel: MOU, FMF, OSP, loan guarantees, missile defence, intelligence sharing, in today's dollars

claims.text: CRS RL33222 (28 May 2025): US has provided 'over $6 billion' for Iron Dome batteries, interceptors, co-production and maintenance; Table 5 lists Iron Dome $6,075.281m, Iron Beam $1,200m (FY2024 supplemental), and US missile-defence funding for Israel FY2006–FY2025 totalling $14,816.853m

CRS RL33222: under a Special Billing Arrangement Israel may use national cash reserves for FMS costs beyond the MOU's funding amounts or duration; if no new MOU is reached and Congress does not appropriate FMF, Israel would have to pay for existing contracts with national funds, find other financing or terminate contracts; Israel's MOD reportedly spends about one-third of annual FMF on direct commercial contracts; Israel cannot use accrued interest for procurement inside Israel; P.L. 119-4 s.11208(c) reauthorizes loan guarantees through 2030

1992 loan guarantees: Congress authorized $10bn for loans tied to Israel's effort 'to resettle and absorb immigrants', in annual increments of $2bn over five years; 1993–97 settlement reductions $1,358.8m less $585m security offset = net $773.8m, $9,226.2m available

2003 loan guarantees: $9bn over three years; reductions of $289.5m and $795.8m (total $1,085.3m); as of 2025 Israel had issued $4.1bn in US-backed bonds and might still be authorized to issue up to $3.814bn; authorized through end of FY2030; JVL says Israel has never defaulted and paid the US fees, so the cost to US government was zero unless default
BLS: CPI-U index level 336.940 (1982-84=100) in September 2026; 334.980 in August 2026

Book's arithmetic (CPI-U, Sept 2026 = 336.940): 1985 aid $3.68bn = ~$11.5bn today; 1992 guarantees $10bn = ~$24.0bn; 2003 guarantees $9bn = ~$16.5bn; CRS $298bn (2024$) = ~$320bn; $3.8bn fixed in 2016 is worth ~$2.7bn in 2016 prices by Sept 2026 (~29% erosion); Costs of War $21.7bn ≈ $23.3bn

Guardian (Snowden documents), via Al Jazeera 12 Sept 2013: NSA agreed a secret deal with Israel for routine sharing of raw intelligence, including unfiltered telephone and internet data on US citizens; the undated memorandum does not require NSA to remove US-person information and reportedly places no limits on Israel's use; Israel must 'destroy upon recognition' communications to or from US government officials; reached in principle March 2009; NSA said US-person information is handled under procedures designed to protect privacy

6 Feb 2019: Israel's MOD and the US DoD confirmed US Army purchase of two Iron Dome batteries (12 launchers, two radars, two battle management centres, 240 interceptors) for $373m ($289m redirected 2019 funds + $83.9m FY2020) as interim cruise-missile defence; Rafael developed it, Raytheon US marketing rights (2011) and 2014 co-production
